doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Birth, parents and her two brothers
summary: Horn gives her birthplace, her parents' names and origins, and her two brothers, neither a musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Were you born at home, or in the hospital, and if so, which hospital?
I was born in Gallagher Hospital. My mother could tell me better. Gallagher Hospital in Northwest [D.C.].
What were your parents‘ names, and what are or were their occupations?
My mother is Grace Louise Horn; I‘m sorry, Grace Louise Saunders. My dad is Ernest Joviet [phonetic] Horn.
Were your parents native Washingtonians? If not, where were they from?
My mother‘s a native Washingtonian. My father is from East St. Louis. My mother‘s from Ivy City, Northeast, which is not too far from where we are now, Ivy City.
Do you have any siblings, any brothers or sisters?
Have two brothers, and that‘s it.
And in what order are you all?
I‘m the oldest one. Ernie is the big one. I‘m the oldest, Ernie is next, and Dale is the next Horn. Yes, he‘s the baby.
Are either one of them musicians?

No. No, they‘re not. I wanted them to do something, but however, my oldest brother is just . . . maybe he‘s about . . . good lord, he‘s about twenty minutes away from here, and he‘s an adjudicator with the government, and the baby brother is just a baby brother. [laughs]
